proof_review: Principal le x is the principal upward profile; transitivity proves it is upward.
ObservedPrincipal is the upward saturation of the observed part of the principal profile; its agreement at B uses reflexivity and transitivity.
The universal agreement premise in the necessity lemma is exactly the antecedent being derived from, not circularly assumed in the final iff.

Applying agreement to principal profiles and their observed saturations produces intermediate factor witnesses. Joint monotonicity lowers their sum to the observed generators; transitivity preserves feasibility.
The universal restriction identity gives observed principal factors directly; its necessity direction genuinely does not require monotonicity.
The two iff theorems and their combination establish all three equivalent predicates corresponding to Section 7.
Reflexivity/transitivity and joint monotonicity are sufficient. No finiteness, identity, associativity, commutativity, or antisymmetry is silently used.
scope: Manually formalized Theorem 1 core equivalences, under weaker preorder/monotone-operation assumptions than the ordered commutative monoid statement. Not literal generated-certificate replay. Nucleus/quantale consequences, group/refund corollaries, and selector results are not formalized here.

explicit_final_preorder_audit.verdict: PASS: necessity is valid for every reflexive/transitive relation, with no antisymmetry or B-saturation hypothesis.
explicit_final_preorder_audit.reason: Principal profiles and their observed upward saturations remain upward and agree at B in any preorder. The proof recovers observed representatives a,c with x <= a and y <= c, not equalities a=x or c=y. Therefore no antisymmetry, quotient representatives, or saturation of B is needed.
explicit_final_preorder_audit.nonantisymmetric_unsaturated_control: On a two-element set with the universal preorder, every pair is related and B may be a singleton. Upward profiles are only empty or full; observing that singleton distinguishes them. Factor-domination holds using that singleton representative for both factors, despite B not being saturated. This corroborates the theorem and shows why a literal B=whole-group corollary would need separate antisymmetry/saturation assumptions.
explicit_final_preorder_audit.closure_scope: product_upward_of_trans explicitly takes only a transitivity hypothesis on le; it asserts closure for arbitrary input profiles. The base agreement theorem does not itself assert closure for an arbitrary relation. No antisymmetry is used.
explicit_final_preorder_audit.implicit_parameter_and_flag_audit: Both source files have autoImplicit=false. Elaborated @ theorem types were printed and checked: only M, add, le, B and the displayed reflexivity/transitivity/monotonicity or universal-agreement premises occur. Ordinary Profile/Upward/Product/restriction/criterion definitions add no assumptions. No custom axiom, sorry/admit, unsafe declaration, partial definition, or implementation override occurs.
explicit_final_preorder_audit.axiom_scope: The kernel dependency audits report no axioms. This does not erase theorem hypotheses; the hypotheses are the explicit parameters shown by the accompanying type audit. Importing Std adds no extra proof assumption to these checked declarations.
